newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: C&P Homes 96 net in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: C&P Homes 96 net in line with expectations.

text.p: C&P Homes Inc, the nation's largest housing developer, said on Wednesday its after-tax profit in 1996 rose by 36 percent to 2.730 billion pesos from 2.011 billion pesos in 1995 from robust housing sales.
Its real estate sales in 1996 increased by 28 percent to 9.406 billion pesos from 7.326 billion pesos.

Analysts said the figures were in line with expectations and the company could see profits growth of 22 to 25 percent to 3.3 to 3.4 billion pesos this year on the back of vigorous demand for housing by the low and middle-income groups.
"It was within target despite delays in the release of funds from the United Home Lending Program (UHLP)," said Colbert Nocom, an analyst of ING Barings Securities.
UHLP is the government's low-cost housing programme which has just been restructured.

"1996 was a challenging year for the company, said Manuel Villar, chairman of C&P Homes. "We are quite happy with our performance and look forward to even better things in the coming years especially in light of the government's renewed commitment to low cost housing as evidenced by the recent restructuring of the UHLP.

ING Barings' Nocom said the company was able to meet its income targets due to a shift to more middle-income housing projects. Demand for middle-range housing in the Philippines had been spurred by higher incomes and the fact that banks were more willing to finance property purchases.
Carolle Kabigting, research head of Peregrine Securities, said her profit forecast for C&P Homes this year was on the higher end at 3.89 billion pesos.
"Last year was a difficult year. Now it should improve," she said, saying the release of funds from the UHLP would now be shortened after a delay of almost six months last year.
Though the company met its earnings targets, analysts are worried the company may have incurred a huge amount of receivables from clients in the process.
But C&P's Villar said "C&P ended 1996 with a strong balance sheet. Total capitalisation at the end of 1996 was in excess of 15 billion pesos."
He said the company settled its short-term debt after issuing a three billion-peso long-term commercial paper late last year which would give the company flexibility to pursue its expansion projects.
He said the company is in the process of forming a new unit, C&P Centers Inc, which will undertake community commercial development projects such as small shopping malls.
